Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"A demonstrated undeclared material dependency, missing required totality declaration or non-total operation violates the F_D contract and yields falsified or refusal(constraint) under the applicable assessment. For this fixture a complete assessed record carries subject, basis,
standing, producer, obligation/version, authority and invalidators. Exact
local keys `report:S`, `report:F`, `report:I` resolve those records. An
independent copy preserves all required fields and the preceding policy
readout. The pointer `candidate-v1` alone maps every report to the same
bytes/identity; S and I then require different continuations, falsifying
its sufficiency for that consumer. Adding a type name alone cannot repair
missing standing.

The acquisition model takes three report keys and the explicit booleans
accessible, target-present and basis-current. Its complete eight-row oracle
per key is: all four inaccessible cases return `inaccessible`; of the four
accessible cases, both absent-target cases return `missing`, the present but
old-basis case returns `stale`, and only the present/current case returns the
qualified record as `resolved`. This yields 24 tested cells. Unavailable,
missing and stale targets yield no usable record and keep the dependent
sufficiency claim unsupported; their actual gap, invalidation, refusal or
residual follows the consuming operation's owner, not a universal result
mapping added by this fixture. The executable also checks that resolution
does not mutate the record store and that valid readouts survive.

These access flags and version comparisons model an acquisition boundary;
they are not observed filesystem, transport or human-handover behavior.
The currentness test covers the declared basis-version invalidator only.
Other material invalidators require their own scoped evidence. Logical review
checks the human handover and required residual meanings; actual use remains
unperformed. A hash-based realization would additionally state its collision,
authenticity and access assumptions; no digest alone proves semantic

A model `M_b` is a valid model of `a_c` under signature `Sigma`, written
`M_b satisfies a_c[Sigma]`, only when (P6, P1):

1. `Sigma` and the exact `a_c` basis resolve;
2. every record satisfies AC-001 through AC-009;
3. every claimed closure, projection, overlay, transformation, judgment
   and composition satisfies its applicable law, and every claimed functor
   application satisfies AC-015 and its bound kind's §5 contract;
4. interpretation fidelity and residual dispositions bind the exact
   subject;
5. structural evaluation and semantic acceptance remain distinct and both
   required where claimed; and
6. all evidence, provenance, invalidation and re-entry coordinates
   resolve.

A checker may decide the structural subset. No generic checker may claim
the semantic or authority subset unless the model supplies an exact lawful
decision contract for it (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F6.%20Interpretation%20and%20models%2FAC-019%20Valid%20model","start_line":1170}],"label":"Valid-model obligations"}}}

`v_copy` accepts lists of length at most two over `{0,1}` and fuel in
`{0,1,2}`. It copies one element per fuel unit; only a complete copy is its
candidate. It terminates after at most two copies. `v_sorted` accepts lists
of length at most three over `{0,1}` and the same fuel. It inspects one
adjacent pair per fuel unit, stopping at the first inversion, when every
pair has been checked, or when fuel ends. It terminates after at most two
comparisons. Its one declared outcome is a closed assessment report containing
the exact input/basis, inspected-pair evidence and any residual; such a
report can carry the `assessment_exhausted` stop with its indeterminate
result. The stop/report is one declared outcome; its availability to an
enclosing step is assessed separately.

| Selected application and observation | Assessed predicate and result | Work result | Signature and traversal stop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_copy([0,1],1)` retains prefix `[0]`, with no complete candidate | Complete copy is available: falsified | `incomplete` → falsified for output availability | `copy_exhausted` maps to falsified, cause fuel ended before the required output |
| `v_sorted([0,1,0],1)` inspects `(0,1)`, with the second pair unexamined | Whole list is sorted: indeterminate on admitted inspected-pair evidence | `candidate_ready` → satisfied for the closed report and transition evidence being available only | `assessment_exhausted` maps to indeterminate, cause performed assessment has insufficient evidence |
| An activated assessing step spends its budget in setup and never invokes `v_sorted` | No assessment result | `incomplete` → falsified for the step's own output availability; the unperformed assessment remains residual work | No traversal application exists and therefore no `v_sorted` judgment or stop exists; the enclosing step retains its own stop and cause |

The two declared exhaustion stops have different predicates and parent core
values. Neither maps to satisfied. A report's availability and its assessed
predicate are not one judgment. Lists of length zero or one are sorted
without inspecting a pair. An observed inversion falsifies sortedness even
when later pairs remain unexamined. No result is inferred from a planned
invocation. These are distinct bounded traversals, not totality proofs for
an unbounded operation. The setup-before-invocation row is a logical-review
case under ACTIVATION §3, not a result of the executable example.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#Deterministic%20contracts%20and%20sufficient%20observations%2FExhaustion","start_line":56},{"end_line":1679,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md","quote":"### Resource limits

A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

- Declaration. A limit applies to an activation only where its intake,
  its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).

  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.

Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"label":"F_D eligibility"}}}

It never silently changes an incomplete task into satisfied.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1679,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md","quote":"### Resource limits

A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

- Declaration. A limit applies to an activation only where its intake,
  its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding
  declares it, because a resource control applies only through a selected
  frame and its owning scope
  ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4 Frame-set selection](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)).
  A declared limit states its unit and the boundary over which it is
  measured: which inputs, actors, processes and repeated reads it counts.
  No universal quota, budget or measurement gate follows.
- Measurement. A declared limit is measured in its unit over its boundary
  where the obligation it serves needs the measurement; consumption
  outside the boundary is recorded as not measured, and no claim against
  the limit covers it. A context limit bounds the material held in active
  context at once, including material acquired during the activation, so
  the bytes supplied at its start, the cumulative bytes it acquires,
  counting repeated reads, and the bound on what it holds at once are
  reported separately; §2 step 3 refines this for the measurement of the
  selected context before it is read. Measures that answer different
  questions, such as the cost components of Cost is selected above, are
  reported separately.
- Exhaustion. Pressure on a declared limit never licenses omitting or
  truncating a material obligation or input. Before a limit would be
  exceeded, the activation refines the task, sequences activations,
  reassigns the work to an actor whose limits fit, or stops with the
  applicable value of §3, naming the limit, such as `incomplete` where
  bounded execution ends first; a stop keeps the unresolved outcome
  ([§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops). Enlarging a limit re-enters the
  owner of the grant or binding that set it.
- Values. The value of each limit, and the units and boundaries the
  selected environment can measure, are set by the selected execution
  binding, which binds this law; for a build tenant that binding is the
  one [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding) defines.
  A value is stated before the activation it limits.
- Standing. An activation that stays within its limits is not thereby
  adequate, and an actor's larger limits grant no authority and waive no
  invariant (P2, P6).

Purpose and material relation: the configuration (§1), context
construction (§2) and frame qualification
([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)) rely on resource
limits, so the law for declaring, measuring and honouring them is stated
once in tier 1, and only their values are left to the execution binding.
The material relation is whether an undeclared, unmeasured or exceeded
limit is read as fitting, or forces a silent omission. The rule applies
RF-014's prohibition of silent omission, REFERENCE_FRAME §4's rule that a
resource control applies only through a selected frame, and UP-014's
selection rule.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F6.%20Cost%20and%20proportionality%2FResource%20limits","start_line":1627},{"end_line":634,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### AC-007 Constraint and refusal

Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
returns one value of the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
coerced to satisfied (P5, P6). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

Constraint results. The outcomes of a constraint's judgment map for the
predicate "the constraint's predicate holds for its governed subject on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

Operation outcomes. A closure (AC-010), a projection (AC-011), the
structural admission of a record, model or carrier, the application of a
transformation (AC-013) and an interpretation (§6) each end in their
declared result or in one of the stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` that
this member writes. Where this member says that a condition refuses, the
operation returns `refusal` naming the condition; the record, model or
carrier is not admitted, and nothing is dropped silently. Each outcome
maps for the predicate "the operation yields its declared result on the
exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| declared result | satisfied | the closure, the projection with its boundary, the admission, the proposed successor `M_b_prime*` or the proposed model `M_subject*` is returned on the exact basis; a proposed successor or model establishes that it is available, never its acceptance or admission (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) |
| `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |
| `gap` | invalid_basis | the result needs a member, reference, resolution or declaration whose resolution on the basis is still open: the declared relation that resolves it has not yet decided it, as for an external resolution not yet evaluated; the result is undefined on this basis until it is supplied. A reference evaluated to no target is dangling and refuses (AC-003): a local reference with no record in the model's closed population, and an external reference whose declared resolution has been evaluated and yields no target |
| `refusal(constraint)` | falsified | every refusal that is not `refusal(basis)`: the refusal names a demonstrated violation of a declared law of this member or a constraint of its signature by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment, including a missing record family (AC-001), a dangling reference (AC-003) and an application without its traversal (AC-015), or it names no condition of the basis; the violation or other defect it names is the counterexample |
| `refusal(basis)` | invalid_basis | the refusal names one or more conditions of the basis the operation acts on and no demonstrated violation of a declared law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment: a seed set, relation family, required-edge semantics, basis or scope that is not exact; a fixed point that is not finite and unique; an input model, subject or carrier whose exact identity, basis or admission is not established; or mixed bases with no composite-basis relation (AC-006) |

The cause is part of a refusal's value, because a refusal would otherwise
map to falsified or to invalid_basis according to its cause, and a refined
value maps to exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
Refinements). A refusal that names a demonstrated violation of a declared
law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or
application under judgment is `refusal(constraint)`, whatever condition of
the basis it also names. The basis condition is recorded with the refusal
and reported beside it as its own `invalid_basis` result, which names the
basis repair and answers the predicate of the evaluation that the
condition leaves without a supporting basis, never the operation-outcome
predicate that the refusal answers
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Predicates travel). A refusal that names only conditions of the basis is
`refusal(basis)`. A violation inside an input that the operation acts on
as its basis is a condition of the basis for that operation, not a
violation by what it judges, as the projection below shows. Purpose and
material relation: a demonstrated violation is a known failure, which
survives every join only as a `falsified` result, so a basis condition
named beside it neither hides the failure nor discards its counterexample,
and the basis repair stays named (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results,
Survival; P5, P6). A basis mismatch inside a model or a record, a
relation's qualifier record included, is mixed bases with no
composite-basis relation (AC-006): a coordinate of the model or record
binds, or a reference in it resolves on, a basis that the governing basis
relation does not admit, as a wrong-basis reference of AC-003 does. It is
a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.
One defect can bear on two predicates: a model that violates AC-001 is
`refusal(constraint)` in the structural admission that judges it and
`refusal(basis)` in a projection over it, and each outcome answers its own
predicate. An operation that was not applied has no outcome. A stop `gap`
is a closed result with the value invalid_basis; it is not the absence of
a result that
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
records as a gap. A signature's stop contract and a traversal record map
stops of their own under §5.

Purpose and material relation: a
constraint result or an operation's stop combines with results of other
members only through the one core, so a refusal, a hold or a gap is
neither read as success nor mistaken for another case; and a closure or
projection that is not established has the value invalid_basis here, as
the activation outcome `closure_unresolved` of
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation) has for its own
predicate (P5, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-007%20Constraint%20and%20refusal","start_line":536}],"label":"Predicate-relative exhaustion"}}}

Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.

[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919}],"statement":"A demonstrated undeclared material dependency, missing required totality declaration or non-total operation violates the F_D contract and yields falsified or refusal(constraint) under the applicable assessment. `v_copy` accepts lists of length at most two over `{0,1}` and fuel in
`{0,1,2}`. It copies one element per fuel unit; only a complete copy is its
candidate. It terminates after at most two copies. `v_sorted` accepts lists
of length at most three over `{0,1}` and the same fuel. It inspects one
adjacent pair per fuel unit, stopping at the first inversion, when every
pair has been checked, or when fuel ends. It terminates after at most two
comparisons. Its one declared outcome is a closed assessment report containing
the exact input/basis, inspected-pair evidence and any residual; such a
report can carry the `assessment_exhausted` stop with its indeterminate
result. The stop/report is one declared outcome; its availability to an
enclosing step is assessed separately.

| Selected application and observation | Assessed predicate and result | Work result | Signature and traversal stop |

| `v_copy([0,1],1)` retains prefix `[0]`, with no complete candidate | Complete copy is available: falsified | `incomplete` → falsified for output availability | `copy_exhausted` maps to falsified, cause fuel ended before the required output |

A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

  its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding
  declares it, because a resource control applies only through a selected
  frame and its owning scope
  ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4 Frame-set selection](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)).
  A declared limit states its unit and the boundary over which it is
  measured: which inputs, actors, processes and repeated reads it counts.
  No universal quota, budget or measurement gate follows.
- Measurement. A declared limit is measured in its unit over its boundary
  where the obligation it serves needs the measurement; consumption
  outside the boundary is recorded as not measured, and no claim against
  the limit covers it. A context limit bounds the material held in active
  context at once, including material acquired during the activation, so
  the bytes supplied at its start, the cumulative bytes it acquires,
  counting repeated reads, and the bound on what it holds at once are
  reported separately; §2 step 3 refines this for the measurement of the
  selected context before it is read. Measures that answer different
  questions, such as the cost components of Cost is selected above, are
  reported separately.
- Exhaustion. Pressure on a declared limit never licenses omitting or
  truncating a material obligation or input. Before a limit would be
  exceeded, the activation refines the task, sequences activations,
  reassigns the work to an actor whose limits fit, or stops with the
  applicable value of §3, naming the limit, such as `incomplete` where
  bounded execution ends first; a stop keeps the unresolved outcome
  ([§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops). Enlarging a limit re-enters the
  owner of the grant or binding that set it.

  selected environment can measure, are set by the selected execution
  binding, which binds this law; for a build tenant that binding is the
  one [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding) defines.
  A value is stated before the activation it limits.
- Standing. An activation that stays within its limits is not thereby
  adequate, and an actor's larger limits grant no authority and waive no
  invariant (P2, P6).

construction (§2) and frame qualification
([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)) rely on resource

once in tier 1, and only their values are left to the execution binding.

limit is read as fitting, or forces a silent omission. The rule applies
RF-014's prohibition of silent omission, REFERENCE_FRAME §4's rule that a
resource control applies only through a selected frame, and UP-014's
selection rule.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F6.%20Cost%20and%20proportionality%2FResource%20limits","start_line":1627}],"statement":"Incomplete copying falsifies the availability predicate and returns incomplete. An a_c interpretation of these assurance relations represents their
material obligations and dependency relationships. Its fidelity and the
acquired views that project it follow
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §6](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#6-interpretation-and-models)
and [Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).
It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a
stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked
structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.
An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to
establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.
No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is
selected (P1, P6).

Assessment of these assurance relations demonstrates the applicable
positive, negative and unresolved cases in [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md),
including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection
that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence.
Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and
observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove
the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain
unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their
governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).

Assessment of these owners and their consumers follows
[EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations) and
[§7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method).
Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate
evidence within the applicable conformance and qualification criteria;
these obligations do not make each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).

construction results to the obligations they support, expose shared
errors, and direct reassessment to affected claims while retaining

Inputs are `assess_S`, `assess_F`, `assess_I` and `advance`. From U an assess
input records that report; from any assessed state it is refused as already
assessed, preserving state. `advance` preserves state and is allowed only
from S; it returns `block_unassessed`, `block_falsified` or
`block_indeterminate` from the other states. This is the complete transition
and decision rule for every state/input pair. There is no reset input in Γ.
A different contract can permit reassessment or re-entry.

The weak observation “satisfied assessment exists” maps U, F and I to false
and S to true. U and I nevertheless require incompatible first-assessment
decisions. Thus no decision function over that observation can preserve the
fixed policy. In a human handover, “not approved” similarly fails to say
whether to perform the first assessment or preserve a completed undecidable
assessment and follow its declared continuation.

standing, permitted first assessment and advance decision are preserved.
The program checks all 16 one-step cells and every length-four input
sequence from every state. Exact one-step preservation with the closed
domain and identical next-state basis also composes by induction to every
finite sequence in this model. Approximate models have no such automatic
bound.

no state aggregation, not evidence of compression, minimum context,
cross-task context selection, Markov sufficiency outside Γ, or cheaper

Traversals and functor kinds

A traversal is a typed contract (P4a, P6):

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

The traversal record is this member's own concept. A same-spelled term
owned by a profile, a realisation or a runtime is not imported by nominal
equality and does not specialise this record except through a declared
binding under that owner's authority (§9; P3, P1).

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities (P3):

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity,
`X_v` and `Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is
its closed stop algebra. `Omega_v` is a refinement of the core result
algebra of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): it adds no
core value, and each of its stop values maps to exactly one core value,
never to `satisfied`. A stop this member writes, `hold`, `gap`,
`refusal(constraint)` or `refusal(basis)`, has the meaning and the core
value that AC-007 gives it. The signature's stop contract declares any
further stop value with the one core value it maps to, and may refine a
stop value by cause. A traversal record's `stop_states` binds the stop
mapping of that traversal, exactly one core value for each stop value; it
may refine a value of the signature's stop contract further by cause for
that traversal. Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`. A
different core value needs a different parent value, which only the member
that owns the parent declares; for these four stops that member is this
one. Neither the stop contract nor a traversal's `stop_states` raises a
result's standing (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: one stop of one
traversal has one core value, so its consumers cannot read it two ways,
and no refinement gives a stop another core value, so a violated
constraint never becomes a case that the evidence merely cannot decide.

- `F_D` classifies total deterministic processing under an exact traversal
  contract. An application declares `f_B:D_B->Outcome_B`, its closed logical
  domain, exact basis, all material computational state and dependencies,
  and its termination argument. For every domain input it terminates with
  exactly one declared outcome. Closed domains may be infinite when
  termination and outcome determination are established. Open-world
  semantic choice and undeclared clock, filesystem or global dependencies
  are outside this contract (P3, P4a, P6).

  Here B is the exact basis of v, D_B is its declared logical input domain
  X_v (including material state and resource inputs), and Outcome_B is the
  declared result-or-stop domain Y_v | Omega_v. The function f_B determines
  one such outcome, including a stop with its closed report where declared;
  that report and its stop are not two outcomes. An enclosing step's output
  availability remains a separate predicate.

  State-dependent processing declares input state and the meaning of its
  returned next state and value. Refusal and exhaustion retain their cause
  and evaluated predicate. The signature and traversal bind each stop to
  exactly one core value, never satisfied; an exhausted tag alone supplies
  no mapping. Construction availability and assessment retain their
  separate predicates and results, and an unperformed assessment has no
  result. A fuel-bounded operation is distinct from the potentially
  divergent operation it bounds. A deterministic decision or effect proposal
  establishes no physical completion, runtime admission, permission or
  quality (P5, P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

The actor, the executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are
different coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure` and
other named domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P` or `F_H`.
Different traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity,
semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence (P3, P6).

Classifying an operation as F_D grants no semantic, evaluation, operation
or decision authority. This is the kind-specific application of
[AC-005](#ac-005-authority-conservation) and
[FOUNDATIONS Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds): the exact
operation contract and admitted grant determine its permissions and
consequences. Consumers apply this boundary to their own operations.

Evaluation-operation profile. An operation declared to evaluate an unchanged
subject identifies that subject, admissible reads, witness or log outputs,
permitted writes, stops and results, authority and invalidation conditions.
It preserves the judged subject and does not perform the domain construction
it judges. Separately authorized persistence of a witness does not perform
the judged domain construction. A construction or mutation needs its own
operation contract and grant; reporting a changed subject's property as the
original subject's property violates this evaluation contract (P6, P3).

Closedness concerns dependencies material to the computation, not complete
world knowledge. This kind's totality is stronger than total handling of
conditions in [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement).
Unbounded work is not automatically `F_P` when a totality argument is missing.
The calculus does not classify every executable process as one of its kinds.
A new non-total deterministic process is outside qualifying F_D. A route to
an F_D claim is a separately identified bounded successor with its own
domain, outcomes, dependency closure and termination argument; a fuel bound
is one possible construction. This proves nothing about the unbounded
original. Other work remains governed by its selected operation and execution
basis without being asserted to be a qualifying a_c application.
Existing operations enter this edition only through the evidence-sensitive
[migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration). The
[finite examples](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md) distinguish construction,
assessment, proposed effects and three predicate-specific exhaustion cases.

"Functor kind" is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does
not by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model that claims
categorical functor laws carries the demonstration that
[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment, requires of
every categorical claim (P6, P1).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds","start_line":919},{"end_line":1115,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### AC-016 Typed composition

Two traversals compose only when the first result type and judgment
satisfy the second traversal's exact domain and preconditions (P4a):

```text
F_K2[w] compose F_K1[v]
```

Composition retains both traversal identities, intermediate results,
judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. It cannot
flatten probabilistic proposal, deterministic construction or evaluation and human
decision into one undifferentiated operation. `a_c` prescribes no
universal `F_P -> F_D -> F_H` sequence; each application owns its lawful
topology (P4a, P4b, P6). FOUNDATIONS §3 P4a consumes this law.

A deterministic constructor feeding a deterministic evaluator still has
two exact traversal identities and retains both results and stops. A claimed
projection of their continuation follows the consumer-relative sufficiency
law in [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation); composition
alone establishes neither adequate observations nor a Markov property.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F5.%20Traversals%20and%20functor%20kinds%2FAC-016%20Typed%20composition","start_line":1095}],"statement":"Compose only when the first result type and judgment satisfy the second exact domain and preconditions. Preserve both identities, intermediate facts, judgments/evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. Keep probabilistic proposal, deterministic construction or evaluation and human adjudication distinct; no universal F_P→F_D→F_H sequence is prescribed, and a common kind implies no common operation identity or authority.","uncertainty":""},"refusal":"urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:stop:no-execution-or-acceptance","scope":["urn:a-c:generation:ba37e2825e4e3c758a5cfaec:scope:source-corpus"]}}

It never silently changes an incomplete task into satisfied.","exceptions":[],"grounding":[{"end_line":1679,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md","quote":"### Resource limits

A resource limit bounds a resource that an activation consumes: context,
attention, wall time, spend, human effort, communication or a machine
resource (P0). This subsection owns the law for every such limit. It sets
no value (P0, P2, P5, P6):

- Declaration. A limit applies to an activation only where its intake,
  its actor's capability envelope or the selected execution binding
  declares it, because a resource control applies only through a selected
  frame and its owning scope
  ([REFERENCE_FRAME §4 Frame-set selection](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#frame-set-selection)).
  A declared limit states its unit and the boundary over which it is
  measured: which inputs, actors, processes and repeated reads it counts.
  No universal quota, budget or measurement gate follows.
- Measurement. A declared limit is measured in its unit over its boundary
  where the obligation it serves needs the measurement; consumption
  outside the boundary is recorded as not measured, and no claim against
  the limit covers it. A context limit bounds the material held in active
  context at once, including material acquired during the activation, so
  the bytes supplied at its start, the cumulative bytes it acquires,
  counting repeated reads, and the bound on what it holds at once are
  reported separately; §2 step 3 refines this for the measurement of the
  selected context before it is read. Measures that answer different
  questions, such as the cost components of Cost is selected above, are
  reported separately.
- Exhaustion. Pressure on a declared limit never licenses omitting or
  truncating a material obligation or input. Before a limit would be
  exceeded, the activation refines the task, sequences activations,
  reassigns the work to an actor whose limits fit, or stops with the
  applicable value of §3, naming the limit, such as `incomplete` where
  bounded execution ends first; a stop keeps the unresolved outcome
  ([§1 Transitions](#transitions), Stops). Enlarging a limit re-enters the
  owner of the grant or binding that set it.
- Values. The value of each limit, and the units and boundaries the
  selected environment can measure, are set by the selected execution
  binding, which binds this law; for a build tenant that binding is the
  one [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding) defines.
  A value is stated before the activation it limits.
- Standing. An activation that stays within its limits is not thereby
  adequate, and an actor's larger limits grant no authority and waive no
  invariant (P2, P6).

Purpose and material relation: the configuration (§1), context
construction (§2) and frame qualification
([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)) rely on resource
limits, so the law for declaring, measuring and honouring them is stated
once in tier 1, and only their values are left to the execution binding.
The material relation is whether an undeclared, unmeasured or exceeded
limit is read as fitting, or forces a silent omission. The rule applies
RF-014's prohibition of silent omission, REFERENCE_FRAME §4's rule that a

selection rule.","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ACTIVATION.md#ACTIVATION%2F6.%20Cost%20and%20proportionality%2FResource%20limits","start_line":1627},{"end_line":634,"path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","quote":"### AC-007 Constraint and refusal

Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
returns one value of the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
coerced to satisfied (P5, P6). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

Constraint results. The outcomes of a constraint's judgment map for the
predicate "the constraint's predicate holds for its governed subject on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

Operation outcomes. A closure (AC-010), a projection (AC-011), the
structural admission of a record, model or carrier, the application of a
transformation (AC-013) and an interpretation (§6) each end in their
declared result or in one of the stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` that
this member writes. Where this member says that a condition refuses, the
operation returns `refusal` naming the condition; the record, model or
carrier is not admitted, and nothing is dropped silently. Each outcome
maps for the predicate "the operation yields its declared result on the
exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| declared result | satisfied | the closure, the projection with its boundary, the admission, the proposed successor `M_b_prime*` or the proposed model `M_subject*` is returned on the exact basis; a proposed successor or model establishes that it is available, never its acceptance or admission (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) |
| `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |
| `gap` | invalid_basis | the result needs a member, reference, resolution or declaration whose resolution on the basis is still open: the declared relation that resolves it has not yet decided it, as for an external resolution not yet evaluated; the result is undefined on this basis until it is supplied. A reference evaluated to no target is dangling and refuses (AC-003): a local reference with no record in the model's closed population, and an external reference whose declared resolution has been evaluated and yields no target |
| `refusal(constraint)` | falsified | every refusal that is not `refusal(basis)`: the refusal names a demonstrated violation of a declared law of this member or a constraint of its signature by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment, including a missing record family (AC-001), a dangling reference (AC-003) and an application without its traversal (AC-015), or it names no condition of the basis; the violation or other defect it names is the counterexample |
| `refusal(basis)` | invalid_basis | the refusal names one or more conditions of the basis the operation acts on and no demonstrated violation of a declared law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment: a seed set, relation family, required-edge semantics, basis or scope that is not exact; a fixed point that is not finite and unique; an input model, subject or carrier whose exact identity, basis or admission is not established; or mixed bases with no composite-basis relation (AC-006) |

The cause is part of a refusal's value, because a refusal would otherwise
map to falsified or to invalid_basis according to its cause, and a refined
value maps to exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
Refinements). A refusal that names a demonstrated violation of a declared
law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or
application under judgment is `refusal(constraint)`, whatever condition of
the basis it also names. The basis condition is recorded with the refusal
and reported beside it as its own `invalid_basis` result, which names the
basis repair and answers the predicate of the evaluation that the
condition leaves without a supporting basis, never the operation-outcome
predicate that the refusal answers
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Predicates travel). A refusal that names only conditions of the basis is
`refusal(basis)`. A violation inside an input that the operation acts on
as its basis is a condition of the basis for that operation, not a
violation by what it judges, as the projection below shows. Purpose and
material relation: a demonstrated violation is a known failure, which
survives every join only as a `falsified` result, so a basis condition
named beside it neither hides the failure nor discards its counterexample,
and the basis repair stays named (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results,
Survival; P5, P6). A basis mismatch inside a model or a record, a
relation's qualifier record included, is mixed bases with no
composite-basis relation (AC-006): a coordinate of the model or record
binds, or a reference in it resolves on, a basis that the governing basis
relation does not admit, as a wrong-basis reference of AC-003 does. It is
a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.
One defect can bear on two predicates: a model that violates AC-001 is
`refusal(constraint)` in the structural admission that judges it and
`refusal(basis)` in a projection over it, and each outcome answers its own
predicate. An operation that was not applied has no outcome. A stop `gap`
is a closed result with the value invalid_basis; it is not the absence of
a result that
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
records as a gap. A signature's stop contract and a traversal record map
stops of their own under §5.

Purpose and material relation: a
constraint result or an operation's stop combines with results of other
members only through the one core, so a refusal, a hold or a gap is
neither read as success nor mistaken for another case; and a closure or
projection that is not established has the value invalid_basis here, as
the activation outcome `closure_unresolved` of
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation) has for its own
predicate (P5, P6).","section":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F4.%20Fundamental%20laws%2FAC-007%20Constraint%20and%20refusal","start_line":536}],"label":"Predicate-relative exhaustion"}}}
